goal: 5-10 new technically qualified EXTREME boards from 5 NEW logical cores (N52 on); never pad; the 24 earlier cores are not used
cores: 5 new cores (core_probe.json, seed_<key>.json); every core cell frozen; the generator only adds and moves free blocks and the listed marks

search_budget.order: round 1 = every core with seed 21; stage 2; round 2 = every core with seed 22; stage 2; round 3 (seed 23) ONLY for cores with no accepted board, and only if fewer than 5 boards are accepted after round 2
search_budget.why this budget: Phase 22 spent 48 runs to get 4 boards, and 55 of its 69 candidates died at the overlap pre-filter because the 24 old cores sit next to the bank. New cores should not hit that wall, so the question is whether they qualify at all: 2 seeds per core (10 runs, ~50 min wall clock) answers it per core, and one extra seed for cores that fail is the most a core gets. The 48-run budget is not reused: it bought cores already saturated.

stage2_candidates: unchanged (tools/extreme90_stage2.py): per run up to 2 qualifying clusters (<= 3 cells apart = one cluster), top-scoring board of each; dropped before any report if overlap (occupancy, best of 8 symmetries) >= 0.40 with ANY bank board (N1-N51) or an accepted Phase 23 board, or with a better-ranked candidate of the round
report_budget: at most 20 full reports (tools/ta90_design.gd, one at a time, idle machine), round-robin across families
acceptance (all must hold): ta90_design.gd verdict HUMAN-REVIEW CANDIDATE for target EXTREME (Category A AND B, thresholds unchanged)
every listed mechanic ESSENTIAL: without it unsolvable, or >= 2 distinct mistakes fewer, or >= 3 decision steps fewer
overlap < 0.40 with every bank board and every accepted Phase 23 board; at most 1 accepted board per CORE; at most 3 per family

the core's critical dependency must survive in the accepted board (checked by hand against core_probe.json and recorded: the frozen cells guarantee the cells, the report's counterfactuals show the mechanics still matter)
exact TIME UP continuation incl. UNDO right after continuing, and the dead-end TIME UP check (Ta90ContinueCheck / Ta90DeadendCheck --boards)
browser: WebAssembly TIME UP check within the page test's limit, iPhone SE layout
human-fit features: tools/ta90_humanfit.gd is diagnostic only: reported for every candidate, never used to accept or reject (no new cutoff)
never: change a threshold after seeing results
use one of the 24 earlier cores

amendments.when: 2026-10-29, after round 3, before any further report
amendments.what: protocol rule 5 (the core dependency must survive) is applied BEFORE stage-2 candidate selection, by tools/ta90_corecheck.gd (the core rammer rams on the Solver line AND leaving with it is a distinct losing move); stage 2 then takes up to 2 clusters per run from the preserving boards, exactly as before
amendments.why: the top-scoring K4 cluster (K4_TOGGLE_s22_1) bypassed its core and was rejected by rule 5 after its report; a check of all 519 qualifying K4 boards of that run shows 343 keep the core - picking by score alone selected the bypass. Rule 5 was meant to define what a candidate of a core IS; applying it first changes no threshold, adds no search run and keeps the 2-cluster and 20-report limits.
amendments.applies_to: runs with qualifying boards: only run_K4_TOGGLE_s22 (every other Phase 23 run had 0 qualifying boards)
